correctness.rationale: For \(d\ge3\), the bipartite cube adjacency operator has top singular value \(d\) and nonconstant singular norm \(d-2\). A selected induced matching has \(k\) endpoints on each parity side and exactly \(k\) crossing edges, so the centered-indicator inequality yields \(k\le2^{d-2}\). At equality the two centered sign vectors lie in the coordinate Walsh eigenspaces, with opposite coefficients. A linear form on \(\{\pm1\}^d\) taking only values \(\pm1\) has one nonzero coefficient, giving exactly the \(2d\) coordinate-parity constructions. The constructions partition edges and imply uniqueness of strong edge coloring and frozen maximum-matching exchange. Two differently structured exhaustive programs were executed, agreeing in dimensions 2-4 and with a further dimension-5 check.

value.rationale: A complete, uniform equality-case classification for an established infinite family is substantially stronger than the numerical induced-matching upper bound. It determines every optimal strong edge-color partition up to renaming and shows that all distinct optimal induced matchings are edge-disjoint and exchange-isolated. These structural consequences are not routine corollaries of the cardinality bounds and provide a natural rigidity principle for the standard hypercubes; dimension two supplies a sharp exchange-graph boundary.
